sourcedFrom: SilencerCo Warlock 22 Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. (UNDATED)
cleanIntro: The Warlock 22 is user-serviceable and SilencerCo says so on the page: the baffle stack comes out and goes back in without a workshop. Rimfire fouling is lead and unburnt powder, so this is a can that genuinely needs the interval keeping. ⛔ Take it off the gun before any of it comes apart.

steps.title: Firearm unloaded and the action OPEN before the can moves
steps.action: Open the action and see that the firearm is visibly clear of ammunition — before the silencer goes on and before it comes off. A suppressed gun is quieter, not safer, and the book says so in as many words.
steps.quote: Before installing the silencer on the host firearm, be sure that the firearm is unloaded and the action is opened so that the firearm is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Warlock 22 Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — WARNING

steps.title: ⛔ NO GAP at the shoulder — check the fit before firing
steps.action: This is the check that prevents a baffle strike. The thread mount must be FULLY shouldered against the barrel with no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the mount. If there is a gap, the silencer does not go on the gun that day.
steps.aside: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc. DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed silencer.
steps.quote: The thread mount must be fully shouldered on the barrel. There should be no visible gap between the barrel shoulder and the face of the silencer thread mount.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Warlock 22 Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — WARNING

steps.title: ⛔ Re-check tightness every 30 rounds
steps.action: Silencers back off under recoil, and a partly-unthreaded can is how baffle strikes happen. SilencerCo names an interval rather than leaving it to feel: verify the attachment is secure after about 30 discharges.
steps.quote: To ensure your silencer remains secure while firing, it is of the utmost importance that you frequently verify the silencer is securely tightened onto the barrel. We recommend checking the security of the attachment after 30 discharges of the firearm.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Warlock 22 Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — WARNING

steps.title: Caps off, baffle stack out
steps.action: The Warlock's baffles are all identical and click together, so there is no order to get wrong — align each one with the notch in the cone and press until no gap remains. Coming apart is the reverse. ⛔ If the stack is stuck, seat an Allen key into the notch of the cone and pry the end baffle away while holding the rest.
steps.quote: Screw back cap onto either end of the suppressor tube until hand tight. Once back cap is shouldered, slide the baffle stack into the suppressor tube until the stack rests against the back cap.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Warlock 22 Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Assembly & Disassembly

steps.title: Interval: about every 1,000 rounds
steps.action: SilencerCo names a number rather than leaving it to judgement, and adds that a change of ammunition is its own reason to clean — different rimfire loads leave very different amounts behind.
steps.quote: It is recommended to clean the Warlock 22 after 1,000 or fewer rounds.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Warlock 22 Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Maintenance

steps.title: Internals take solvent and light abrasives — test first
steps.action: The internal components can be cleaned with solvents or light abrasive media, and abrasive pads or wire brushes are allowed. ⛔ But test on an inconspicuous spot first: the finish scratches, and once it is gone it is gone.
steps.aside: The use of abrasive pads or wire brushes is acceptable, but a small test should be done on an inconspicuous area to ensure no scratching or damage will occur to the metal finish.
steps.quote: The Warlock 22 internal components (NOT the outer tube) can be cleaned using solvents, or light abrasive media.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Warlock 22 Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Maintenance

steps.title: ⛔ Dry it — and oil the baffles after a water-based cleaner
steps.action: Dry all components thoroughly before reassembling. If you used a water-based cleaner, lightly coat the baffles with oil or another corrosion-resistant product afterwards — water left on a rimfire baffle stack rusts it where you cannot see.
steps.aside: Dry all components thoroughly before reassembling.
steps.quote: If using a water-based cleaner, make sure to lightly coat the baffles with oil or other corrosion-resistant product after cleaning.
steps.cite: SilencerCo Warlock 22 Field Manual — ⛔ No form or revision code is printed in this book. — Maintenance

deepAbsentReason: SilencerCo publishes ONE level of disassembly for this silencer and it is the routine cleaning itself — the strip in the Assembly & Disassembly section is what an owner does every cleaning interval, not an occasional deep service. There is nothing deeper published, and nothing was borrowed: the SEALED SilencerCo cans in this same batch publish LESS, not more, so there is no sibling to take a deeper procedure from even if one were wanted.

cleaning.name: STRIP FIRST
tasks: ⛔ Off the host firearm completely before anything comes apart
Firearm unloaded, action open, chamber checked

cleaning.name: BAFFLES & INTERNALS
tasks: Solvent or light abrasive media on the INTERNALS only
Nylon or plastic bristles; no hard metal scrapers
Everything DRY before it goes back together

cleaning.name: OUTER TUBE
tasks: ⛔ NOT solvent-soaked and NOT ultrasonic — the finish and the serial
Damp cloth or a soft non-abrasive brush
Gun oil restores a discoloured finish

cleaning.name: AFTER A WATER-BASED CLEANER
tasks: ⛔ Light coat of oil or a corrosion inhibitor on the baffles

reassembly: Back cap screwed onto either end of the tube until hand tight and shouldered.
Baffle stack slid into the tube until it rests against the back cap.
Front cap screwed onto the open end and tightened with the included takedown tool.
⛔ A slight gap between the front cap and the tube is intentional — leave it.
Threaded onto the barrel hand tight, no barrel thread visible, no gap at the shoulder.
fncheck: Reassembled: back cap shouldered, baffle stack seated against it, front cap tightened with the provided tool. ⛔ A slight gap between the front cap and the tube is intentional on these — do not force it closed. Mounted: hand tight, no barrel thread visible, no gap at the shoulder, and re-check after 30 rounds.
